handling.guidance: A row restates the whole role as it stands from date: title, and grade, reports_to, terms and location wherever they are known, not only what changed. A snapshot keeps only the latest row of a series, so a row naming only the change would lose the rest. An acting role or secondment is a row, and the return from it is another row. org is one agreed spelling per organisation across every source and every org type: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the name the person uses for it and not its legal entity (employer and legal_entity carry those). With stint it is the series key, so a typo or a second spelling makes a second employment. date is a local date in Australia/Sydney, wherever the employer is; the Definition reads it in that zone and carries no zone_pointer. When the source knows only the month or the year, date is the first day of that month or year and date_precision says month or year, which the schema holds to (month means a date ending -01, year a date ending -01-01); basis says why the date is believed. Pay is never written here, in any org.employment type: not salary, rate, allowance or bonus. The id is declared in identity_template, <source>:employment/<org>/<stint>/role-changed/<date>, so two role changes cannot share a date: give the later one the later day, or month. Leave id out and Anam fills it; send it and it must match.
handling.label: {/title} ({/org})

schema.description: A change of role within one period of employment: a new title, grade, manager, terms or location. One row in a records file (source records), in the org.employment series, displacing the row before it.

basis.description: Why the date is believed, in the writer's words: the document it rests on, or that it is the person's recollection. Read it before trusting the date.

date.description: The day the role took effect, YYYY-MM-DD, a local date read in Australia/Sydney. When date_precision is month or year, the first day of that month or year. This is the fact time.

date_precision.description: How much of date the source supports. When it is month, date is the first day of that month; when year, the first day of that year. The schema refuses a coarser precision with any other day.

grade.description: The role's grade or band from date, as the employer writes it.

id.description: Identity, composed from the rest by the Definition's identity_template: the source prefix, then employment, the org, the stint, role-changed and the date. A writer may leave it out and Anam fills it; one that sends it must send exactly the composition.

location.description: Where the role is based from date, as written.

org.description: The organisation, in one agreed spelling: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the way a drug has one spelling. The name the person uses for it, not its legal entity, so the same employer is always the same string across every source and every org type. With stint it is the key of the org.employment series, so two spellings are two employments.

reports_to.description: Who the role reports to from date, by name or title, as written.

source_note.description: What the writer saw in the source and how they reached this row. Writer's text, not the source's.

source_time.description: How `date` was read: value is the date or period as the source gave it ("2019-09-30", "Sep 2019", "2019"), zone the zone it is read in, and basis who decided that zone (source when the document names it, configuration when a setting does, assumption when the writer chose Australia/Sydney, the zone this Definition reads date in, with nothing behind it). A date is a local date, so the zone is never the employer's by default. fact_time stays the one UTC instant the gate derives.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.

stint.description: Which period of employment with this org, counting from 1; leaving and rejoining is a new stint. Assigned by the writer. With org it names the org.employment series.

terms.description: The employment terms from date, as written: permanence and hours. Never pay.

title.description: The role's title from date, as written.
